sections.title: Appealing to Presumed Common Ground
sections.content: The discourse particle ugyebár ('isn't it / as you know / surely / right?') signals that the speaker expects the listener to agree with a stated premise. It functions similarly to an English tag question or conversational parenthetical, drawing the listener into shared complicity or mutual understanding.

sections.title: Irony and Conversational Rhythm
sections.content: In satirical and essayistic Hungarian, ugyebár often carries an ironic edge, pointing out an obvious contradiction between official pretension and undeniable reality. It can stand at the beginning, middle, or end of a clause.

sections.title: Communicative Uses of ugyebár
rows: A pesti humor, ugyebár, mindig a legnehezebb időkben volt a legélesebb.
Pesti humor, as we well know, was always sharpest in the hardest times.
Nem gondoltad komolyan, ugyebár, hogy a hivatalos sajtó igazat írt?
You didn't think seriously, did you, that the official press told the truth?
Ugyebár emlékszel még Salamon Béla híres mondására?
You remember Béla Salamon's famous saying, don't you?
A legnehezebb körülmények között, ugyebár, a nevetés jelentette a menedéket.
Under the hardest circumstances, as is well known, laughter meant the refuge.

items.spanish: Az óvóhelyek sötétjében, ugyebár, a fanyar viccek segítettek elviselni a bombázásokat.
items.english: In the dark of the air raid shelters, as we know, wry jokes helped endure the bombings.

items.spanish: A totalitárius hatalom, ugyebár, leginkább a gúnytól és a nevetségessé válástól rettegett.
items.english: Totalitarian power, isn't it true, dreaded mockery and becoming ridiculous above all else.

items.spanish: Ti sem vettétek komolyan a propaganda ígéreteit, ugyebár?
items.english: You didn't take the promises of the propaganda seriously either, did you?

sections.title: B2 Usage Notice
sections.content: Use ugyebár to create rapport or subtle ironic distance. In spoken speech, it can be shortened to 'ugye', but in formal writing and B2 essays, 'ugyebár' is the preferred literary form.
